question: It is possible to carve a flat region into three separate 'lakes', arranged so that every single point on the shoreline borders all three lakes at once.
anchorText: the counterintuitive property that they all have the same boundary

question: If you write the whole numbers 1, 2, 3, ... outward in a square spiral and then mark every prime number, the primes —
choices: cluster tightly near the centre and thin out toward the edges
scatter about with no visible pattern at all
form concentric rings, roughly one prime per ring
line up along striking diagonal streaks
anchorText: primes appear to concentrate along certain diagonal lines

question: Prime numbers thin out as you count higher. Even so, no matter how long a run you ask for — ten primes, a thousand, a million — there exists a set of exactly that many primes spaced at perfectly equal intervals.
anchorText: the sequence of prime numbers contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions

question: Wilson's disease is an inherited disorder in which one metal slowly builds up to poisonous levels in the liver and brain. Which metal?
anchorText: the excess build-up of copper in the body

question: Physicists have not only slowed a beam of light to a crawl — they have brought light to a complete standstill, holding it motionless and then releasing it to travel on again.
The little spinning vanes of a Crookes radiometer — the black-and-white paddles sealed inside a glass bulb — are driven round by the physical pressure of the light striking them.
anchorText: Crookes incorrectly suggested that the force was due to the pressure of light

question: Ordinary lava erupts glowing red-orange at well over 1,000 °C. The lava of Tanzania's Ol Doinyo Lengai — the only volcano of its kind on Earth — is unusual because it is —
choices: even hotter, erupting so fiercely it glows brilliant white
much cooler than any other lava on Earth, barely glowing at all
anchorText: an unusually low temperature and highly fluid type of magma

question: Humans possess a fully working vomeronasal organ — a dedicated sense organ, much like a snake's, for detecting pheromones.
anchorText: there is no reported evidence that human beings have active sensory neurons
